notes: Only original-side n_o, es_value_o and pval_value_o are assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Identity verified from the supplied article title and author block. Rendered PDF page 5 confirms the two-column layout and printed page 603. The locator provides no study/outcome/test discriminator. Study 1 candidates: unadjusted ideology-to-nostalgia b = .10, SE = .03, t(261) = 3.12, p = .002 (exact), R2 = .04; adjusted ideology-to-nostalgia b = .12, SE = .03, R2 = .11, t(259) = 3.62, p < .001; exploratory age r = .12, p = .05 (exact); gender d = 0.46, t(261) = 3.73, p < .001. Also printed: ideology item correlation r = .82, p < .0001; adjusted age b = .07, p = .226 and adjusted gender b = .44, p < .0001. Study 1 reports 263 participants and all completing the same items; 262 is an a priori target, not the observed sample. Studies 2a and 2b report participant counts 200 and 423, respectively. Their page-5 power statements print f2 = .10 and f = .16; these are not interchangeable metrics, and the .10 statement is a design/power assumption rather than a located observed target estimate. Page 604 additionally reports the Study 2a ideology-by-condition endorsement interaction b = .19, SE = .08, t(196) = -2.22, p = .028; this is another candidate, not an identified assigned test. No candidate selected by numeric or row-order matching, no conversion to Cohen's f^2, no N summation, and no analytic N derived from df. All candidate values remain in notes/dispositions; all assigned core values stay null because correspondence is unresolved.
